candidates.explanation: updateByHash ignores conditions.hash. It updates by id only (`{ id: Number(conditions.id) }`), so the refresh token's hash is never compared to the session's current hash. A rotated (old) refresh token still has a valid signature and session id, so the update succeeds again and a new token pair is issued. The document (Mongo) repository filters on both _id and hash, which is the correct behaviour.

fix.description: Include the hash in the update condition: `this.sessionRepository.update({ id: Number(conditions.id), hash: conditions.hash }, { hash: payload.hash })`. Then a stale hash affects 0 rows and the method returns null, so refreshToken throws UnauthorizedException. Also fetch the entity by id after the update.
